question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\sin{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2 \cos{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}.
$$

Substituting, including the required constant factor, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{- 3 \cos{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}}{\sin{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=- \frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate with respect to $u$:

$$
- \frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=- \frac{3}{2}\left(\ln\left|u\right|\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
- \frac{3}{2}\left(\ln\left|\sin{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\right|\right)+C.
$$

Let $u=\tan{\left(4 x \right)} + 2$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4 \sec^{2}{\left(4 x \right)}.
$$

$$
\frac{u-2}{u}=1-\frac{2}{u}.
$$

Substituting, including the required constant factor, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{- \tan{\left(4 x \right)} \sec^{2}{\left(4 x \right)}}{\tan{\left(4 x \right)} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=- \frac{1}{4}\left(\int 1 - \frac{2}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
- \frac{1}{4}\left(\int 1 - \frac{2}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=- \frac{1}{4}\left(u-2\left(\ln\left|u\right|\right)\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
- \frac{1}{4}\left(\tan{\left(4 x \right)} + 2-2\left(\ln\left|\tan{\left(4 x \right)} + 2\right|\right)\right)+C.
$$
